Emma —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline — this is helpful. Short answer: we can get in the neighborhood, but we have a few proposed changes to balance predictability and platform economics. High level proposal from my side:

- Annual escalation cap: Redwood can agree to a ceiling on list price increases applied to per-token rates, but we need a floor (minimum base rate) to protect against sustained low utilization and to preserve reserved capacity economics.
- Minimum-commitment floor: instead of a fixed multi-month floor, we propose a 12-month smoothing corridor that guarantees effective discount bands if ACME hits a 12-month rolling commit; otherwise we offer pro-rated credits.
- True-up mechanics: agree to 60-day post-quarter true-ups via credits for overage, with an explicit billing credit schedule and a cap on aggregate credits per year (to avoid open-ended exposure).

I'll loop Legal and Finance to finalize the exact contract language. Proposed next steps: I will send a Redwood redline and a short mutual action plan (timeline + DocuSign link) by EOD Wed so you can review. If ACME is comfortable with a capped credit liability and a rolling-commit smoothing corridor, we should be able to meet your two-week target.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Mina —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed ACME's redline and drafted recommended language (see attached ExhibitD_price-stability_redline.docx). Summary of the changes I recommend:

- "Price Stabilization Rider" (Exhibit D): define terms ("Escalation Cap", "Stabilization Floor", "True-Up Window"). We should accept an Escalation Cap at 12% rather than 10% (offers better protection given cloud cost dynamics); if Sales wants 10% to close, note this as commercial concession for approval.
- Stabilization Floor: language that sets an effective minimum blended rate based on the greater of (a) 85% of then-current list per-token rate or (b) the customer's committed effective rate averaged over the prior 12 months — this protects reserved capacity economics.
- True-up: 60-day post-quarter true-up by credit only, with an annual aggregate credit cap equal to 6% of committed ARR. Credits are applied to future invoices over the next two quarters.
- Exceptions: exclude price changes required by third-party licensing or extraordinary compute cost spikes (we should define a "Compute Cost Adjustment" threshold and require notice).

If Sales is comfortable with a 12% cap vs 10%, we reduce legal friction. Aditya — please confirm the 6% credit cap modelling and whether two-quarter credit application is acceptable for cashflow.

I attached the redline and a tracked-change paragraph you can drop into Exhibit B or D depending on commercial preference.

Regards,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
